The '''2025 FIFA Club World Cup final''' was the final match of the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]], the 21st edition of the premier competition for men's club [[association football|soccer]] teams organized by [[FIFA]]. The match was played at [[MetLife Stadium]] at the [[Meadowlands Sports Complex]] in [[East Rutherford, New Jersey|East Rutherford]], [[New Jersey]], near [[New York City]], on July 13, 2025. It was contested between English club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and French club [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]]. This final was the first since [[2000 FIFA Club World Championship final|2000]] to be contested by two teams from the same confederation—the only previous Club World Cup to feature multiple teams from the same association or country—and the first ever to feature two European teams.

Chelsea won the match 3–0 for their second [[FIFA Club World Cup]] title and first under the new format.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lev |first1=Jacob |last2=Snell |first2=Patrick |title=Cole Palmer leads Chelsea to dominant victory over PSG to win FIFA Club World Cup |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/07/13/sport/chelsea-psg-fifa-club-world-cup-final-spt |website=CNN |access-date=July 14, 2025|date=July 14, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=DeBono |first=Matt |date=July 15, 2025 |title=How Chelsea completed their trophy set |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/club-world-cup/usa-2025/articles/chelsea-first-title-wins |access-date=August 14, 2025 |website=[[FIFA]]}}</ref> Meanwhile, PSG's loss cost them the opportunity to become the first team to achieve a [[Sextuple (association football)#Seventh and eighth titles|septuple]], since it won the [[continental treble]] before the tournament and won the [[2025 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]], [[2025 FIFA Intercontinental Cup|FIFA Intercontinental Cup]], and [[2025 Trophée des Champions|French Super Cup]], respectively, after the tournament.

==Venue==
[[File:Metlife stadium (Aerial view).jpg|thumb|right|Aerial view of [[MetLife Stadium]] in 2014, the host venue for the final|alt=Aerial image of a large American football stadium with three tiers of stands and no roof; the stands are empty and several pieces of equipment are parked around its exterior.]]

The host venue for the final was [[MetLife Stadium]] in [[East Rutherford, New Jersey|East Rutherford]], [[New Jersey]], {{convert|5|mi|km}} west of [[New York City]].<ref name="BBC-Stadium">{{cite news |date=September 28, 2024 |title=Fifa names 12 US stadiums for 2025 Club World Cup |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c17lw80kpdvo |work=[[BBC Sport]] |accessdate=October 1, 2024}}</ref> FIFA announced the final's host venue on September 28, 2024. MetLife Stadium is also scheduled to host the [[2026 FIFA World Cup final|FIFA World Cup final]] in July 2026.<ref>{{cite news |date=September 28, 2024 |title=2025 Club World Cup final to be at MetLife Stadium, site of 2026 World Cup final |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/soccer/2025-club-world-cup-final-to-be-at-metlife-stadium-site-of-2026-world-cup-final/ |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=October 1, 2024}}</ref> The stadium had primarily been used by the [[New York Giants]] and [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) since it opened in 2009.<ref>{{cite news |last=Blum |first=Ronald |date=February 4, 2024 |title=2026 World Cup final will be played at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/2024/02/04/2026-world-cup-schedule/1c65f7a0-c3a0-11ee-bbc9-9b5ca9b20779_story.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |agency=Associated Press |accessdate=October 1, 2024}}</ref> It had a listed capacity of 82,500 seats and previously hosted [[Super Bowl XLVIII]] in 2014 and the [[Copa América Centenario final]] in 2016.<ref name="NYTimes-NYNJ">{{cite news |last=Waldstein |first=David |date=February 9, 2024 |title='New York New Jersey' Got the World Cup Final. Now Comes the Hard Part. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/02/09/nyregion/new-york-new-jersey-world-cup-final.html |work=The New York Times |url-access=limited |accessdate=October 1, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Anzidei |first1=Melaine |last2=Rampling |first2=Ali |date=February 4, 2024 |title=New Jersey's MetLife Stadium wins the 2026 World Cup final |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5241468/2024/02/04/world-cup-final-2026-new-jersey/ |work=The Athletic |url-access=subscription |access-date=October 1, 2024}}</ref>

==Entertainment==
On June 9, 2025, FIFA and [[Global Citizen (organization)|Global Citizen]] announced the headliners for the halftime show which included [[J Balvin]], [[Doja Cat]], [[Tems]], [[Coldplay]] and [[Emmanuel Kelly]] (later added on July 12),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://inside.fifa.com/organisation/news/origin1904-p.cxm.fifa.com/emmanuel-kelly-club-world-cup-halftime-show-x-factor-chris-martin |title=Emmanuel Kelly's awe-inspiring journey to FIFA Club World Cup™ Halftime Show |publisher=Fédération Internationale de Football Association |website=FIFA.com|accessdate=13 July 2025|date=12 July 2025}}</ref> a prelude to the halftime show for the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://inside.fifa.com/organisation/media-releases/origin1904-p.cxm.fifa.com/j-balvin-doja-cat-tems-club-world-cup-final-halftime-show-global-citizen |title=J Balvin, Doja Cat and Tems to headline the inaugural FIFA Club World Cup™ Final Halftime Show, produced by Global Citizen |publisher=Fédération Internationale de Football Association |website=FIFA.com|access-date=June 15, 2025 |date=June 9, 2025}}</ref> In addition, [[Robbie Williams]] and [[Laura Pausini]] performed a pregame show at the stadium.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://inside.fifa.com/organisation/media-releases/origin1904-p.cxm.fifa.com/robbie-williams-laura-pausini-build-up-club-world-cup-final |title=Robbie Williams and Laura Pausini to lead unforgettable build-up to FIFA Club World Cup™ final match |publisher=Fédération Internationale de Football Association |website=FIFA.com|accessdate=13 July 2025|date=12 July 2025}}</ref>

===Chelsea===
Chelsea qualified for the tournament as the winners of the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FIFA Council confirms key details for FIFA Club World Cup 2025™ |url=https://inside.fifa.com/organisation/fifa-council/media-releases/fifa-council-confirms-key-details-for-fifa-club-world-cup-2025-tm |publisher=Fédération Internationale de Football Association |website=FIFA.com |access-date=July 11, 2025 |date=December 17, 2023}}</ref> They entered the tournament having recently won the [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League]], becoming the first club to [[UEFA club competition records and statistics#List of teams to have won the main European club competitions|win all four major European trophies]] and all three of the current European competitions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/news/0299-1dde1ba33803-6370dd142717-1000/ |title=Real Betis 1–4 Chelsea: The Blues complete the set with Conference League success |website=UEFA.com |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=May 28, 2025 |access-date=May 28, 2025}}</ref> They were drawn into group D alongside [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]], [[Los Angeles FC]], and [[Espérance Sportive de Tunis|Espérance de Tunis]]. In the opening match, Chelsea beat Los Angeles FC 2–0, with goals coming from [[Pedro Neto]] and [[Enzo Fernández]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea 2–0 LAFC: Chelsea win their Club World Cup opener at largely empty stadium in Atlanta |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c626y880d67t |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=June 16, 2025}}</ref> Chelsea were defeated 3–1 by Flamengo in the second match, a result that meant Chelsea would at best finish second in the group.<ref>{{cite news |title=Flamengo 3–1 Chelsea (Jun 20, 2025) Game Analysis |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/724444 |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=ESPN |date=June 21, 2025}}</ref> In the final game, Chelsea were up against fellow knockout stage hopefuls Espérance de Tunis. Chelsea won 3–0, with goals from [[Tosin Adarabioyo]] and [[Tyrique George]], alongside new signing [[Liam Delap]]'s debut goal. The result secured Chelsea's place in the knockout stage as the second placed team in Group D.<ref>{{cite news |title=Club World Cup LIVE: ES Tunis vs Chelsea – match updates & stats |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cx2vlrjlkw0t |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=June 25, 2025}}</ref>

In the round of 16, Chelsea faced [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], the winners of Group C. Chelsea gained the lead via a free-kick goal from captain [[Reece James (footballer, born 1999)|Reece James]], before the match was halted due to lightning for nearly two hours.<ref>{{cite news |title=Breaking down Chelsea's extraordinary four-hour Club World Cup match that was delayed by severe weather |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6453216/2025/06/28/chelsea-benfica-highlights-delay/ |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=New York Times |date=June 28, 2025}}</ref>  A late [[Ángel Di María]] penalty sent the game to extra time, where Chelsea goals from [[Christopher Nkunku]], Pedro Neto, and [[Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall]] saw the Blues come out 4–1 winners.<ref>{{cite news |title=Benfica vs Chelsea LIVE: Club World Cup score, stats & updates |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0rvz95exd4t |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=June 28, 2025}}</ref> In the quarterfinals, Chelsea faced [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] in a rematch of the [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup final]], which Chelsea had previously won 2–1. The result would be identical. [[Cole Palmer]] opened the scoring with his first goal of the tournament, before [[Estêvão Willian]] scored the equalizer in what would be his final appearance for Palmeiras before moving to Chelsea. Chelsea's winner came via an own goal by Palmeiras goalkeeper [[Weverton (footballer, born 1987)|Weverton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Palmeiras 1–2 Chelsea: Blues reach Club World Cup semi-final despite Estevao's goal against his new club |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c4g2290v9yvt |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=July 5, 2025}}</ref> In the semifinals, Chelsea faced another Brazilian side [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]], the last remaining non-European team in the tournament. Chelsea won 2–0 with a brace by newly signed and registered [[João Pedro (footballer, born 2001)|João Pedro]], a product of the Fluminense academy.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea's Pedro hits debut double in Club World Cup semi to down Fluminense |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2025/7/8/chelseas-pedro-hits-debut-double-in-club-world-cup-semi-to-down-fluminense |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=Al Jazeera |date=July 8, 2025}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
Paris Saint-Germain qualified for the tournament via the UEFA ranking pathway as one of the best ranked European teams. They entered the tournament as the reigning European champions, having recently won the [[2024–25 UEFA Champions League]]. They were drawn into group B alongside [[Atlético Madrid]], [[Botafogo FR|Botafogo]], and [[Seattle Sounders FC]]. In the opening match, Paris Saint-Germain beat Atlético Madrid 4–0 with two first half goals from [[Fabián Ruiz]] and [[Vitinha (footballer, born February 2000)|Vitinha]] to go along with two late goals from [[Senny Mayulu]] and [[Lee Kang-in]].<ref>{{cite web |title=PSG turn up the heat in LA sunshine |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/club-world-cup/usa-2025/articles/paris-saint-germain-atletico-madrid-highlights-match-report |publisher=Fédération Internationale de Football Association |website=FIFA.com|access-date=July 11, 2025|date=June 15, 2025}}</ref> In the second match, Paris Saint-Germain faced Botafogo, the reigning South American champions. In an extraordinary upset, the South Americans would win 1–0, with the only goal scored by [[Igor Jesus (footballer, born 2001)|Igor Jesus]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Botafogo stuns UCL champs PSG at FIFA Club World Cup |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2025/6/20/botafogo-upset-ucl-champs-psg-at-fifa-club-world-cup |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=Al Jazeera|date=June 19, 2025}}</ref> In the third game, Paris Saint-Germain faced Seattle Sounders FC at their home stadium, winning 2–0 with goals from [[Khvicha Kvaratskhelia]] and [[Achraf Hakimi]]. The result secured Paris Saint-Germain's place in the knockout stage as the winner of group B, ahead of both Botafogo and Atlético Madrid — both of which also had six points — on head-to-head goal difference.<ref>{{cite news |title=PSG 2–0 Seattle Sounders: European champions seal place in last 16 |date=June 23, 2025 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ce83v612mv0t |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In the round of 16, Paris Saint-Germain faced [[Inter Miami CF]], an American team featuring former Paris Saint-Germain player [[Lionel Messi]]. Paris Saint-Germain won with a comfortable scoreline of 4–0, with brace from [[João Neves]] and a goal from Hakimi to go with a Miami own goal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rampant PSG send Messi and Miami home |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/club-world-cup/usa-2025/articles/paris-saint-germain-inter-miami-highlights-match-report |publisher=Fédération Internationale de Football Association |website=FIFA.com|access-date=July 11, 2025|date=June 29, 2025}}</ref> In the quarterfinals, Paris Saint-Germain faced [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in a rematch of the [[2020 UEFA Champions League final]], which Bayern had won 1–0. This time, Paris Saint-Germain would win 2–0 with goals from [[Désiré Doué]] and [[Ousmane Dembélé]]. The match also saw Bayern player [[Jamal Musiala]] getting seriously injured due to a clash with Paris Saint-Germain goalkeeper [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Christe |first1=Andrew Timothy |title=Jamal Musiala says 'no one to blame' for serious leg injury at Club World Cup |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/sport/football/2025/Jul/10/jamal-musiala-says-no-one-to-blame-for-serious-leg-injury-at-club-world-cup |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=The New Indian Express |date=July 10, 2025}}</ref> while two Paris Saint-Germain players — [[Willian Pacho]] and [[Lucas Hernández]] — were sent off and earned two match suspensions each.<ref>{{cite news |title=FIFA hands two-match bans to PSG duo after Bayern red cards |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/fifa-hands-two-match-bans-to-psg-duo-after-bayern-red-cards-41346559 |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=OneFootball |date=July 11, 2025}}</ref> In the semifinals, Paris Saint-Germain faced [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] featuring former Paris Saint-Germain player [[Kylian Mbappe]]. Once again, Paris Saint-Germain would win comfortably, 4–0, with a brace from Ruiz and a Dembélé goal in the first half to go along with a late [[Gonçalo Ramos]] goal.<ref>{{cite news |title=PSG 4–0 Real Madrid: European champions set up Club World Cup final against Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c74z0zxq825t |access-date=July 11, 2025 |date=July 9, 2025 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

==Pre-match==
[[File:DHS Secretary Kristi Noem Attends FIFA Club World Cup 2025 Championship Match - 54653678957.jpg|thumb|right|View of the match during the first half]]

Present at the match was [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]], who was accompanied by [[First Lady of the United States|First Lady]] [[Melania Trump]], as well as [[List of presidents of FIFA|FIFA president]] [[Gianni Infantino]] and his partner.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bonilla |first=Melani |title=Trump attends FIFA Club World Cup final |date=July 14, 2025 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/07/13/sport/video/trump-attends-fifa-final-vrtc |access-date=July 14, 2025 |website=CNN}}</ref>

==Match==

===Summary===
The defending UEFA Champions League champions Paris Saint-Germain were heavily favored by bookmakers before the final.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Richman |first=Darren |date=2025-07-13 |title=PSG vs Chelsea Club World Cup final odds, prediction: Can the Blues prevent another French triumph? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6486422/2025/07/13/psg-chelsea-club-world-cup-final-odds-prediction/ |access-date=2025-08-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Chelsea scored first in the 22nd minute, after [[Cole Palmer]]'s low shot reached in the far left corner off an assist from [[Malo Gusto]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-07-13 |title=Chelsea beats PSG 3-0 for Club World Cup title as Palmer scores twice and sets up third goal |url=https://apnews.com/article/club-world-cup-final-chelsea-psg-score-bd3b0fb78c27cace1e8f7f6c555cb9c8 |access-date=2025-08-05 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref> Eight minutes later, Palmer scored a second goal, once again low into the same far left corner. He became the first English player to score two goals in a Club World Cup final.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-13 |title=Chelsea 3-0 PSG LIVE REACTION: Palmer stars as Blues claim CWC victory |url=https://talksport.com/football/3365821/chelsea-vs-psg-time-commentary-free-stream-channel-club-world-cup-final/ |access-date=2025-08-05 |website=talkSPORT |language=en-gb}}</ref> Chelsea's press produced a third goal in the 43rd minute, which Palmer assisted and [[João Pedro (footballer, born 2001)|João Pedro]] scored lifting the ball over the advancing goalkeeper. PSG finished the game with 10 players after [[João Neves]] received a straight red card for pulling [[Marc Cucurella]]'s hair in the 85th minute. With the victory, Chelsea had won every international competition it had entered in history.<ref>{{Cite news |title=How Chelsea completed their trophy set |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/club-world-cup/usa-2025/articles/chelsea-first-title-wins |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250716081641/https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/club-world-cup/usa-2025/articles/chelsea-first-title-wins |archive-date=2025-07-16 |access-date=2025-08-05 |website=www.fifa.com |language=en}}</ref>
